messages:
ella: FYI: p95 streaming latency spiked after yesterday's rollout, looks like SSE chunking got coalesced. Observed on canary and a perf CI regression.
reza: Seen it too. Nice repro on local with small payloads — chunks arrive only at the end now. p95 up ~120ms.
maya: Any recent PRs touching streaming/io or toolcall serialization?
alex: I suspect the HTTP writer change in 9c4b7d8 where we switched to the buffered writer to reduce syscalls. It added a 64KB buffer and only flushes on newline/close.
ella: That matches. Streaming responses are often small deltas (toolcall tokens, short assistant chunks). Buffering would add latency until buffer fills or request ends.
reza: Also noticed KV cache invalidation on toolcall paths — toolcall wrapper now reinstantiates a lightweight serializer which touches the cache key namespace, causing cold misses. Could be compounding latency.
maya: Perf CI output: "perf-ci: streaming_latency_p95: baseline=78ms current=198ms (+153%)" — failure triggered.
perf-ci: Failed job: runtime/streaming/p95_check — see: https://ci.internal/perf/17951
ella: Can someone run a bisect? I can start. Hypothesis: 9c4b7d8 (buffered writer) + a9f1c2e (toolcall serializer change) together cause visible regression.
alex: Start bisect on canary branch. I can revert 9c4b7d8 first as a quick test. If that improves streaming we know buffering is first-order.
reza: Meanwhile I'll profile KV cache misses around toolcall. Running `perf record` on the handler to capture miss hotspots.
maya: Minimal repro script below — helps iterate quickly:
```bash
# send 100 short streaming requests
for i in {1..100}; do
  curl -s -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -d '{"prompt":"short"}' https://canary.internal/v1/stream | cat >/dev/null &
done; wait
```
ella: Reverted 9c4b7d8 on canary and re-ran the script. p95 dropped back to ~85ms. So buffering is the main offender.
alex: Confirmed. That means 9c4b7d8 is the culprit for the streaming buffering. We still should investigate a9f1c2e for KV churn but lower priority.
reza: KV profiling shows a spike in namespace lookups around toolcall metadata deserialization — looks like we now stringify metadata and touch cache keys twice. Patch incoming.
maya: Proposed immediate mitigation: add a 'priority flush' path for streaming small-chunk responses and bypass the buffered writer for StreamingHandler when Content-Type is `text/event-stream` or `application/stream+json`. Pseudo-patch:
```go
// if small-chunk streaming, force immediate flush
if headers.Get("Content-Type") == "text/event-stream" || headers.Get("X-Stream-Mode") == "immediate" {
  w = unbufferedWriter(original)
} else {
  w = bufferedWriter(original)
}
```
ella: Also add a short-timer flush for buffered path (e.g., flush every 5ms if buffer has any data) to avoid blocking short streams.
alex: I'll prepare a minimal revert for 9c4b7d8 to unblock rollout, and a follow-up that implements the priority flush + timer.
perf-ci: Queued re-run: runtime/streaming/p95_check on canary (build 1795123500).
deploy-bot: Rollout queued for canary: revert/9c4b7d8 -> pending approval.
ella: If revert passes canary perf, we'll ship revert to stable and then land a more robust guard (priority flush + unit tests + perf test).
reza: Patch for toolcall serializer to avoid touching KV namespace twice is ready, will open MR after revert lands.
maya: Add an integration perf test that sends many tiny streaming events and asserts flush latency < 120ms p95. Saves us from regressing again.
alex: Agreed. I'll add the test in runtime/perf and a CI gate.
ella: Thanks all. Keeping this thread as the rollout blocker chain. @deploy-bot please notify when revert goes to stable. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Noted. Will post updates in this thread.
